_provenance.notes: Sitka Sound Pacific herring is one of Alaska's most valuable per-pound fisheries — the sac roe fishery targets pre-spawning herring for the Japanese kazunoko (salted herring roe) market. A single season lasts 20-60 minutes at peak (a true 'opening' fishery). ADF&G uses acoustic surveys, spawn surveys, and age composition to set the annual harvest guideline. The Exxon Valdez 1989 spill does NOT directly affect Sitka Sound herring (which is in Southeast Alaska, ~900 miles from PWS).

kazunoko_market.description: Japanese market context for Sitka Sound sac roe — the primary demand driver
kazunoko_market.notes: Sitka Sound sac roe (kazunoko — salted herring roe) is a traditional New Year's food in Japan considered good luck. Japanese buyers bid up prices in good years. The 1990 Japanese asset bubble collapse directly caused Sitka herring roe prices to fall 40% in 3 years. Since the 1990s, Japanese consumption of kazunoko has declined as younger generations eat less traditional foods. ADF&G monitors Japanese market conditions as part of their pre-season planning.
